messages:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing increased GPU kernel ooms on a subset of Dedicated H100 hosts after yesterday's driver+cuda pilot wave. Not full outage but elevated retry rates in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1.
liam: Which kernel/driver combo? logs?
maya: stack traces point at nvcuda + 525.60 driver + CUDA 12.2 combo. NCCL shows timeouts in multi-GPU jobs. sample log: `E NCCL: Unhandled cuda error (700) at cuda_runtime.c:xxx`
andre: Noted. Pilot wave went to 3 pools: rw-dedicated-eu-west1-h100-2, -3 and ap-se1-h100-pool1. All three rolled last night 02:00 UTC.
sasha: Infra metrics: packet drops and TCP retransmits also up on those nodes by ~0.4% — looks like MTU mismatch on a subset of NIC firmware after the driver.
olga: We only flipped driver on nodes with new cudatoolkit. Could be a kernel module ABI mismatch. Which kernel versions are in those pools?
maya: eu-west1: 5.15.0-70; ap-se1: 5.15.0-72 (some older ones at 5.10 in the pool too).
infra-oncall: I'm seeing a small bump in Dedicated capacity alerts — autoscaler kept trying to add nodes but many requests errored with `failed to initialize driver`.
liam: Can we pause rollout to remaining pools?
maya: Paused. wave-2 and wave-3 were not started. Only wave-1 (the pilot we did) completed.
andre: Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) disable multi-GPU scheduling on affected pools (force single GPU tasks) 2) switch routing policy to fallback model variant on hosted until we confirm stability 3) prepare rollback to previous driver (524.x).
sasha: Agreed on disabling multi-GPU scheduling. I'll push a pod-affinity override to kube scheduler for those node selectors. Command: `kubectl label nodes -l pool=rw-dedicated-eu-west1-h100-2 no-multi=true`
olga: Rollback plan needs a timed window and capacity check. Rolling driver downgrade will take ~15m per node with reboot. We have ~120 nodes across the three pools. If we do parallel `n=20` waves, that'll still take hours and spike preemption costs.
liam: Can we hotpatch kernel module (nvidia.ko) instead of full driver? Risky.
maya: We verified that the nv-kernel module built against 525 is incompatible on some 5.15 subpatches — hotpatching may cause further instability. Downgrade safer.
andre: Cost note: keeping degraded nodes increases GPU waste due to retries; estimated additional billing ~ $3.2k/day if not rolled back. Rolling carries operational cost too.
infra-oncall: Proposing action window: start rollback in 45 minutes for low-traffic hours in EU, staged by AZ and node-group. I'll coordinate with SRE on oncall rotations.
liam: Let's list exact steps for rollback runbook: 
- Lock wave (no further upgrades).
- Mark nodes cordon/cordon & drain in batches of 10: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- SSH run: `sudo apt-get remove -y nvidia-driver-525 && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-524 && sudo reboot`
- Post-reboot smoke: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv`
- Re-enable multi-GPU scheduling after 30 min stable.
Make sure we have image cache warm for rescheduled pods.
sasha: I'll create the scheduler label automation and a short circuit to re-enable when `prometheus:dedicated_gpu_errors` falls below 0.1 per minute for 30m.
maya: Also open a support ticket with vendor with kernel logs. Tagging @nvidia-support in SAT channel and uploading `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and dmesg snippets.
deploy-bot: deploybot: wave-2 (driver-525) rollout paused by maya at 1839123470. Reason: observed regressions. :pause_button:
olga: One more thing — some Dedicated customers deploy pinned versions and may see token errors if pods are rescheduled to different capacity. Notify account oncall and support about possible transient throttles.
liam: I'll ping sales-ops and support with a short note to affected accounts in EU/APAC.
andre: After rollback, we should run a stress harness for 4 hours focusing on NCCL multi-GPU paths and 95/99 latency windows. If green, resume a slow wave with kernel-upgrade fence (only nodes on mainline 5.15.0-70).
maya: Agreed. Also let's add a preflight: `modinfo nvidia` hash compare + run a small NCCL allreduce test in isolated pool before allowing multi-GPU scheduling.
infra-oncall: Starting coordination call in 10m in #incident-ops. I'll post runbook snippets and operator assignments.
liam: Thanks — appreciate the quick pause. :thumbsup: 
maya: I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft after the rollback completes.
deploy-bot: deploybot: rollback run queued by infra-oncall at 1839123540. Operators assigned: olga, sasha, liam.
maya: tagging this thread with `incident:driver-compat` and adding to postmortems/ for visibility.
liam: Any objections to adding an automated canary that runs the NCCL mini-bench as part of future driver rollouts?
andre: No objections — high value. Let's do that before wave-2.
maya: OK, action items: olga (execute rollback), sasha (scheduler labels + monitoring thresholds), liam (customer comms + canary test spec), andre (cost calc + stress harness), maya (postmortem).
maya: I'll keep updates in this thread.
